reasons: Overlaps on graph neural networks, machine learning, network science
subject: Interested in your graph representation learning work
body:
Hello Professor Leskovec,

My name is Vinil Polepalli and I am an undergraduate at New York University, pursuing a dual degree in Computer Science at the Courant Institute and Business at Stern. I have been a research intern in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering, where I built protein-ligand graph neural networks for Hsp90 and epichaperome complexes that reached 0.984 ROC AUC separating active from inactive inhibitor candidates.

I read GraphSAGE, and the shift I keep coming back to is from learning a separate embedding per node to learning an aggregation function over a node's local neighborhood, so that embeddings can be produced for nodes never seen during training. That constraint is exactly the one I ran into at MSK. My screening model was trained on 2,574 known compounds and then asked to rank 4,566 generated molecules, most sharing no scaffold with anything in the training set, so a transductive embedding would have had nothing to say about them. What I would want to try is treating a docked protein-ligand pose as the neighborhood to aggregate over, sampling atoms by interaction type from the PLIP fingerprints rather than by graph distance, and then testing whether an inductive encoder holds its enrichment on scaffolds held out of training entirely.

In the past, I have worked on the following related projects:
- Hsp90 inhibitor virtual screening in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering: 4,566 candidates screened at 0.984 GNN ROC AUC and 5x enrichment, 0 Lipinski violations in the top 50: https://hsp90-dashboard.vercel.app/
- Sole author on cVAE-augmented deep learning for pan-cancer RNA-seq classification, about 98% test accuracy across 5 cancer types on TCGA: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02743
- Semantic segmentation for UAV-based environmental monitoring at Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute: 0.88 mean IoU and 0.94 F1 on 25,000 labeled aerial images, sub-100 ms inference across 30 flights

I have extensively used PyTorch and Python in past work, along with molecular docking and graph learning tooling, but have a lot of coding experience and am adaptable to whichever libraries your lab utilizes. Please let me know if there is a fit in your lab.

I would be happy to elaborate on my skills and where I think I can best help out.

Thank you!

--
Vinil Polepalli
New York University | Class of 2029
B.S. Computer Science (Courant) and B.S. Business (Stern)
